**Global Flexible‑Work Policy – 2026 (12‑Month Review)**  

---

## 1. Executive Summary  
This policy defines a uniform framework that allows our 12‑country organization to offer compressed‑week (4‑day) schedules, hybrid‑work, and right‑to‑disconnect rules in a way that respects local labour law, client expectations, and cultural attitudes toward visibility and commitment. It balances equity, operational continuity, and data‑privacy while giving teams the flexibility to thrive in a changing work landscape.

---

## 2. Scope & 12‑Country Footprint  

| # | Country | HQ Office | Timezone(s) | Key Local Employers | Primary Language(s) |
|---|---------|-----------|-------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| 1 | United States | Austin, TX | US/Eastern, US/Pacific |  USF, SF, Seattle | English |
| 2 | United Kingdom | London | GMT / BST | London, Manchester, Edinburgh | English |
| 3 | Australia | Sydney | AEST | Sydney, Melbourne | English |
| 4 | India | Bangalore | IST | Bengaluru, Hyderabad | English, Hindi |
| 5 | South Africa | Johannesburg | SAST | Johannesburg, Cape Town | English, Zulu, Afrikaans |
| 6 | Netherlands | Amsterdam | CET/CEST | Amsterdam, Rotterdam | Dutch, English |
| 7 | Japan | Tokyo | JST | Tokyo, Osaka | Japanese |

*The policy is written in English and translated into the primary languages listed.*

---

## 3. Core Principles  

| Principle | Rationale | Operational Levers |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| **Legal Compliance** | Avoid fines, lawsuits, and reputational risk | Jurisdiction‑specific rule‑sets, automated HRIS validation |
| **Outcome‑First** | Performance defines value, not hours | Key Result Indicators (KRIs) tied to business outcomes |
| **Transparent Visibility** | Counteract “absence = disengagement” biases | Multi‑modal status reporting (written, recorded, live) |
| **Cultural Respect** | Honour local norms of work & leisure | Region‑specific core hours, “visible‑work” tactics |
| **Equity & Inclusion** | Equal opportunity for all offices | Role‑type matrix, pay‑factor comparison, benefits parity |
| **Privacy & Security** | Protect employee & client data | GDPR/CCPA-compliant remote access, data‑residency rules |
| **Continuous Improvement** | Adapt to new laws & market trends | Quarterly audit, data‑driven KPI monitoring |

---

## 4. Legal Compliance Overview  

| Country | Governing Law | Max Weekly Hours | Rest Periods | Overtime Rate | Right‑to‑Disconnect | Data‑Privacy Notes |
|---------|--------------|------------------|--------------|---------------|---------------------|--------------------|
| **United States** | Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) | 40 h (non‑exempt); 50 h for overtime (exempt) | 8 h after 54 h workday | 150 % overtime | No statutory rule; policy‑based | California CCPA, Do‑Not‑Track, cross‑border |
| **United Kingdom** | Working Time Regulations 1998 (UK) | 48 h (avg over 17 weeks) | 11‑h rest + 24‑h break | 1.5 × | Post‑2023 “Right to Disconnect” Act | GDPR |
| **Australia** | Fair Work Act 2009 | 38 h (avg over 4 weeks) | 10‑h rest | 1.5 × | No statutory rule | Privacy Act 1988 |
| **India** | Shops & Establishments Act (varies by state) | 48 h / week (commonly 40‑44 h) | 1‑hr break every 5 h | 1.25‑1.5× | No statutory rule | PDPPA 2018, GDPR‑influenced |
| **South Africa** | Basic Conditions of Employment Act | 45 h / week (max 40 h in any 7‑day period) | 1‑hr break per 5 h | 1.5× | No statutory rule | POPIA 2013 |
| **Netherlands** | Dutch Working Hours Act | 36 h (standard), 44 h (max) | 11‑h rest | 1.5× | No statutory rule | GDPR |
| **Japan** | Labour Standards Act | 40 h / month | 8‑h rest daily | 1.25× | No statutory rule | Act on the Protection of Personal Information |
| **France** | French Labour Code | 35 h / week | 11‑h rest | 25 % overtime | 2023 “Right to Disconnect” | GDPR |
| **Brazil** | Consolidated Labor Laws (CLT) | 44 h / week (40 h + 4 h overtime) | 1‑hr break | 1.5× | No statutory rule | LGPD 2020 |
| **Mexico** | Federal Labor Law | 48 h / week | 1‑hr break | 1.25× | No statutory rule | Data Protection Act |
| **Saudi Arabia** | Labor Law (Royal Decree 2/2020) | 8 h daily, 48 h / week | 24‑h rest | 1.5× | Sharia‑compliant working days | Saudi Data & AI Authority |
| **Kenya** | Labour Act 2007 | 48 h / week | 1‑hr break | 1.5× | No statutory rule | Data Protection Bill |

**Key Takeaway:** The policy sets compressed‑week limits that *never exceed* these statutory maxima. Where a country’s normal weekly cap is 35 h (France, Japan), the policy permits a 32‑h compressed week only if an average of 48 h over 17 weeks (UK) or 38 h over 4 weeks (Australia) is not breached.

| Country | Standard Weekly Hours | Allowed Compressed Hours | Minimum Off‑Days | Rest/Break Notes |

| US | 40 h (exempt) | 32–35 h (if no overtime) | 2 consecutive | 8‑h break after 6 h shift |
| UK | 48 h avg/17w | 32–35 h (if avg ≤48 h) | 2 consecutive | 11‑h rest + 24‑h after 6 h shift |
| Australia | 38 h avg/4w | 32–35 h (if avg ≤38 h) | 2 consecutive | 10‑h rest + 24‑h after 5‑h block |
| India | 45 h/w | 32–35 h (if state law allows) | 1 day (no need to be consecutive) | 1‑hr break per 5 h |
| South Africa | 45 h/w | 32‑35 h (if avg ≤45 h) | 2 consecutive | 1‑hr break |
| Netherlands | 36 h | 32–35 h | 1 day (single) | 11‑h rest |
| Japan | 40 h/m | 32–35 h (if monthly average ≤40 h) | 2 consecutive | 8‑h rest |
| France | 35 h | 32–35 h (requires explicit agreement) | 2 consecutive | 11‑h rest |
| Brazil | 44 h | 32–35 h (if avg ≤44 h) | 1 day | 1‑hr break |
| Mexico | 48 h | 32–35 h (if avg ≤48 h) | 2 consecutive | 1‑hr break |
| Saudi Arabia | 48 h | 32–35 h (if avg ≤48 h) | 2 consecutive | 24‑h rest after 8 h |
| Kenya | 48 h | 32–35 h (if avg ≤48 h) | 2 consecutive | 1‑hr break |

*Every compressed‑week arrangement must be captured in the HRIS “Flex‑Work” module and automatically validated against the table above.*

*Teams are allowed to **rotate** their core window within the 30‑minute band (e.g., 10:00–14:00 or 10:30–14:30) so that they can meet local client peaks.*

### 6.2 Visibility Modalities  

| Modality | When to Use | Tool(s) | Notes |
|----------|-------------|---------|-------|
| **Written Status** | Daily stand‑up, critical updates | Jira, Confluence | Standard in Japan, South Africa |
| **Sprint Demo** | End of sprint | Zoom/Webex, Teams | Preferred in US, UK, Australia |
| **Asynchronous Recording** | Limited bandwidth, remote | Loom, Vidyard, internal recorder | Default for Kenya, India |
| **Live Check‑In** | Ad‑hoc urgent communication | Slack Thread, Teams Chat | 24‑h window during core hour |
| **“Visible‑Work” Snapshot** | Quarterly review | Sharepoint / PowerBI | KPI heatmap for managers |

*All visibility posts must satisfy the **Data‑Privacy** rule: no personally identifying data unless consented.*

| Country | Primary R2D Rule | Allowed Exceptions | Enforcement Tool |
|---------|------------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| US | No statutory rule; policy‑based | Emergency (critical incident, 24‑h response) | Auto‑reply & priority flag |
| UK | Right‑to‑Disconnect Act 2023 | Same as US | Email/Teams auto‑reply, policy sign‑off |
| Australia | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| India | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| South Africa | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| Netherlands | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| Japan | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| France | Statutory | Same as UK | Auto‑reply |
| Brazil | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| Mexico | No statutory rule | Emergency | Auto‑reply |
| Saudi Arabia | Sharia‑compliant working days | Emergency (e.g. health crisis) | Auto‑reply |

*Employees must sign a “R2D Consent” form that records the agreed core hours and emergency allowances. The policy allows an *after‑hours* exception only if the incident is logged in the Incident Management system and the employee’s manager approves.*

## 9. Compensation & Equity  

1. **Base Salary**  
   * Compressed‑week employees retain **full base salary** if they deliver on contractual KPIs and work‑time compliance.  
   * For *internal‑only* roles (e.g., R&D, analytics), a **salary‑multiplier of 0.82** applies if hours dropped below 35 h but output meets expectations.  
   * This multiplier is adjusted quarterly by the Compensation Board to reflect local purchasing‑power parity (PPP) changes.

2. **Benefits Parity**  
   * All employees, regardless of compressed or full‑time status, receive the same health, dental, and pension benefits according to local law.  
   * For countries with no statutory pension, the company offers a *voluntary contribution* equal to 4 % of base salary.

3. **Equity Framework**  
   * The “Compressed‑Week Matrix” aligns eligibility with *role‑type, seniority, and client‑delivery mix*.  
   * Example: Software Engineers, Data Scientists, and Product Managers in any country can request compressed weeks if they have >30 % client deliverables.  
   * Senior leadership positions (VP, Director) are *exempt* from compressed‑week options to preserve executive availability.

4. **Pay‑Factor Review**  
   * Monthly “Pay‑Factor” dashboards compare average hourly earnings by office.  
   * Discrepancies > 10 % trigger a review by Compensation & Region Heads.

---

## 10. Client‑Facing Scheduling & Service Continuity  

| Scenario | Guidance | Role‑Level Impact |
|----------|----------|-------------------|
| **Compressed‑Week Employee on Client‑Critical Day** | • Add an *alternate* or *shadow* team member, or • Re‑schedule client session to a compressed‑week employee’s core day. | Shadow must have same skillset & client history. |
| **Frequent Client Requests** | If more than 2 client‑critical days per month fall outside an employee’s compressed days, the employee must *convert* to a full‑time schedule. | Managed by Regional Sales Ops. |
| **Remote‑Only Delivery** | If a project can be delivered entirely remotely, the employee may take *up to 4* remote days per week without affecting compressed‑week status. | Requires client approval and updated SLA. |
| **Contractual Change** | Any change to compressed‑week status during a client contract requires a *Contract‑Change Request* (CCR) and legal review. | CCR must be signed by both the employee and client’s point‑of‑contact. |

## 11. Governance & Oversight  

| Role | Authority | Escalation | Union / Bargaining |
|------|-----------|------------|-------------------|
| **Chief People Officer (CPO)** | Global policy approval, policy revision authority | Escalate to CEO if >2 disputes in 6 mo | Liaison with EU & Australian unions |
| **Regional HR Lead** | Local compliance validation, local policy adjustments | ESCALATE to CPO if conflict with local law | Handles union negotiations |
| **Legal Counsel** | Contracts, regulatory risk | Escalate to CPO | Advises on union‑related legalities |
| **Finance & Payroll** | Compensation calculation, tax compliance | Escalate to CFO if audit flag | Supports union agreements |
| **Compliance Lead** | Audit, risk monitoring | Escalate to COO | Cross‑regional compliance taskforce |
| **Team Lead / Manager** | Day‑to‑day decisions, pilot approval | Escalate to Regional HR Lead | Facilitates union communication at team level |

**Escalation Path for High-Impact Dispute**  
1. Manager → Regional HR Lead  
2. Regional HR Lead → CPO  
3. CPO → CEO (for policy‑change)  
4. If union involvement → Legal Counsel & Union Representative

## 13. Pilot Review & Rollback Metrics  

| KPI | Threshold | Trigger | Escalation |
|-----|-----------|---------|------------|
| **Team Delivery Time** | > 15 % increase vs baseline | Review by Regional Ops | Escalate to CPO |
| **Employee Satisfaction (EHS) score** | < 70 (scale 0‑100) | Quarterly survey | Escalate to HR Lead |
| **Client SLA Breach** | > 2 breaches/month | Incident log | Escalate to Sales Ops |
| **Compliance Audit Findings** | > 5 risk items | Annual audit | Escalate to Legal Counsel |
| **Remote Data Leakage** | > 0 incidents | Security alert | Escalate to Compliance Lead |

*If any threshold is breached, the policy triggers a **“Rollback”** to the previous 5‑month compliance baseline within 30 days, accompanied by a “Recovery Action Plan” documented in the HRIS.*
